regions.name: Muyinga
regions.title: Muyinga Province
text: Muyinga Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Buhumuza.

regions.name: Kirundo
regions.title: Kirundo Province
text: Kirundo was one of the eighteen provinces of Burundi, in north of the country bordering Rwanda. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Butanyerera.

The economy was mostly based on agriculture, with a dispersed population and few sizable communities. Before 1970 large parts of the province were forested. Migrants from the south then cleared much of the vegetation to create agricultural land, and Kirundo became the breadbasket of Burundi. The civil war from 1993 to 2005 caused agricultural output to drop by more than half. Afterwards, lack of farm inputs, poor infrastructure and shortages of water caused widespread poverty.

regions.name: Ngozi
regions.title: Ngozi Province
text: Ngozi was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Butanyerera.

regions.name: Cibitoke
regions.title: Cibitoke Province
text: Cibitoke Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into the new Bujumbura Province.

regions.name: Kayanza
regions.title: Kayanza Province
text: Kayanza was one of the provinces of Burundi. Its capital city was also called Kayanza. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Butanyerera.

regions.name: Cankuzo
regions.title: Cankuzo Province
text: Cankuzo was one of the provinces of Burundi. Located in the eastern part of the country, the province covered an area of 1,965 km2. The provincial capital was Cankuzo. It was Burundi's least populated province. In 2025, it became part of the new province of Buhumuza.

regions.name: Ruyigi
regions.title: Ruyigi Province
text: Ruyigi Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Buhumuza.

regions.name: Rutana
regions.title: Rutana Province
text: Rutana was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it became part of the new province of Burunga.
It contained the Karera waterfalls, and the Nyakazu Fault.

regions.name: Makamba
regions.title: Makamba Province
text: Makamba was a province of Burundi. The province had a population of 430,899 (2008 census) and covers an area of 1,960 km2.  The provincial capital was Makamba. Makamba had six communes. In 2025, it was merged into the new province of Burunga.

regions.name: Bubanza
regions.title: Bubanza Province
text: Bubanza was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into the new Bujumbura Province.

regions.name: Bujumbura Rural
regions.title: Bujumbura Rural Province
text: Bujumbura Rural Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. It surrounded the former national capital Bujumbura and its provincial capital was Isale. In 2025, the province was merged into the new Bujumbura Province.

regions.name: Bujumbura Mairie
regions.title: Bujumbura Mairie Province
text: Bujumbura Mairie Province was one of the eighteen provinces of Burundi. It consisted entirely of the city of Bujumbura, Burundi's largest city and economic capital. In 2025, it was merged into the new Bujumbura Province.

regions.name: Bururi
regions.title: Bururi Province
text: Bururi was one of the provinces of Burundi. It was formerly Burundi's largest province until the communes of Burambi, Buyengero and Rumonge were transferred to the province of Rumonge when it was created in 2015. In 2025, Bururi was merged into the new province of Burunga.

regions.name: Gitega
regions.title: Gitega Province
text: Gitega is one of the five provinces of Burundi. Its capital is Gitega, which is also the political capital. It has a population of 725,223 as of 2008 and an area of 1,979 square kilometres (764 sq mi).

regions.name: Muramvya
regions.title: Muramvya Province
text: Muramvya Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. The capital city was Muramvya. In 2007 the province was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. In 2025, the province was merged into the new Gitega Province.

regions.name: Mwaro
regions.title: Mwaro Province
text: Mwaro Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. Its capital was Mwaro. In 2025, it was merged into Gitega Province.
Mwaro Province was one of two provinces that were created in 1999 as a result of splitting the Muramvya Province; the other province retained the name of Muramvya.

regions.name: Karuzi
regions.title: Karuzi Province
text: Karuzi Province was one of the provinces of Burundi. In 2025, it was merged into Gitega Province.
